answer: Opportunity-cost staking resists sybils: each identity locks capital in a bond that earns nothing while held, so the sybil tax is the foregone yield that copper could have earned elsewhere over the window — no forfeiture needed. A raven-dark farm of k heads each locks a full bond and gives up k times that yield for the whole horizon, so the drain grows linearly with head count, burning like a slow ember. An honest agent locks once and recovers principal plus the chance to redeploy. Precondition: bond times yield rate over the window exceeds per-head expected gain.
